newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Horn, Vranitzky open Hungary-Austria gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Horn, Vranitzky open Hungary-Austria gas pipeline.

text.p: The 117-km long Hungarian-Austrian gas (HAG) pipeline between Hungary's Gyor and Austria's Baumgarten was officially opened on Tuesday by Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, a MOL spokesman told Reuters.

The pipeline, built by Hungarian oil and gas company MOL and Austria's OMV, has been operational since October 1 when Germany's Ruhrgas AG started supplying Hungarian oil and gas company MOL with natural gas.
The 71-km long Hungarian stretch of the pipeline cost MOL four billion forints while the Austrian part cost 700 million Austrian schillings, MOL said in a statement.
The pipeline has an annual capacity of 4.2 billion cubic metres, it said.
According to an agreement between MOL and OMV, OMV will supply an annual three billion cubic metres natural gas through the pipeline until December 31, 2016, it added.

With this pipeline MOL has started to diversify its gas supply sources. So far 55 percent of Hungary's annual gas consumption of 11 billion to 12 billion cubic metres came from Russia and the rest from domestic sources.
Hungary's annual gas consumption is expected to rise to 15 billion to 17 billion cubic metres by 2010, the statement said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange MOL shares traded at 1,545 forints, down five, at 1209 GMT.
